subject: Urgent: Throttle & 5xx spike after model rollout — rollback playbook
messages:
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] spike in 5xx/429s after last model rollout

Team — monitoring flag: starting ~08:50 PDT we see an abrupt increase in 5xx (up 14x baseline) and 429s (burst to 7x) across the hosted api-perf cluster serving model: model/redwood/v2-quant-kernelA. Error graphs attached. Latency p95 increased from 180ms to 780ms. First anomalies correlate with the midnight (UTC) rollout of quantized build "v2-quant-kernelA".

Current impact: some customers are seeing timeouts and retry storms (client SDK auto-retries compounding 429s). Notable: Acme Corp and FastCommerce have active high-throughput sessions.

Immediate asks:
- can engineering triage and check kernel/quant mismatch? (jonas)
- ops: throttle/rate-limit temporary to reduce retry storms (rishi/aditya)
- AMs: notify impacted customers and suggest disabling aggressive client retries (marissa/stephanie)

Attachments: throttle_metrics_may28.png

-Aditya (oncall)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] spike in 5xx/429s after last model rollout

Thanks Aditya — I’m escalating to execs and paging infra. Jonas, please confirm whether the quantization profile or kernel selection changed in the automated rollout (build tag + kernel selector). If this is model-specific we need an immediate rollback plan and a canary stop.

I will:
- Stand up a 30-min incident huddle in 10 minutes (09:40) — invite list: eng infra, product, AMs, oncall.
- Coordinate a customer-facing note for top impacted accounts (Stephanie/Marissa to co-ordinate).
- Authorize temporary global retry-backoff policy for the hosted API to reduce retry storms (ops).

If rollback is the recommendation, we will revert to v2-quant-kernelB (previous stable) and run a partial canary to validate. Prioritize throughput stability over throughput delta for now.

-Rishi
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acmecorp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] spike in 5xx/429s after last model rollout

Stephanie — we started seeing a large volume of 500s and client-side timeouts starting around 08:52 PDT. Our checkout flow retries twice by default; we had a cascading failure across a handful of high-concurrency customers which caused revenue impact on one APAC campaign. Please advise immediate mitigation and whether rollback is expected.

We need an ETA on a fix and whether we should disable client retries.

—Lisa Gomez
Head of Platform & Integrations, Acme Corp
[lisa.gomez@acmecorp.com]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Root cause hypothesis & rollback checklist

Quick summary after initial triage:
- The rollout changed kernel selection logic in the ops compiler: for certain attention kernel shapes, the scheduler switched to kernelA which under quantized weights shows a pathological slow path on A100 Gen2 for multi-request workloads. This causes increased CPU scheduler waits and higher per-request latency, which in turn triggers client retries that overwhelm front-door routing and produce 429s.

Hypothesis: model-specific serving regression introduced by kernel selection + quant profile mismatch. Not a networking or DB issue.

Immediate proposed actions (ranked):
1) Scoped rollback: pin serving group "api-perf-1" back to model/redwood/v2-quant-kernelB (last known good) — target 30min window for rollback + quick smoke tests.
2) Temp protective measures: enable early-429 backoff at edge for suspected clients, raise per-key concurrency soft limits to slow client throttling loops.
3) Ask AMs to push a short-runbook to top impacted customers recommending disabling client auto-retries and increasing client-side exponential backoff.
4) After-stable steps: reproduce locally with kernelA+quant profile and create a regression test in CI.

I’m attaching a concise rollback checklist and the metrics snapshot.

Attachments: rollback-checklist.pdf, throttle_metrics_may28.png

-Jonas
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acmecorp.com>, John Park <john.park@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: service impact & immediate mitigations

Lisa / John — sorry for the disruption. Quick actions we recommend immediately (we can apply these from our side or you can do them):
- Disable client auto-retry for 30–60 minutes or set max retries=0 in SDK config. This will reduce retry amplification.
- If you control client concurrency to the Redwood API, add a 250–500ms jittered exponential backoff between calls for the next hour.
- We are initiating a rollback to the previous model variant now and will provide status updates in the incident channel.

We will credit impacted request volume as per SLA for the hour(s) affected. I’ll follow up with a short post-incident note and next steps.

-Stephanie
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: postmortem-draft.docx]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acmecorp.com>, John Park <john.park@fastcommerce.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: rollback complete — post-incident next steps

Status update: rollback to model/redwood/v2-quant-kernelB completed at 15:10 PDT. Metrics show 5xx rate reduced to baseline and 429s trending down. Latency p95 back ~200ms.

What we did:
- Scoped rollback on api-perf-1 and monitored canary traffic for 30 minutes.
- Enabled temporary edge backoff policy to limit retry amplification.
- AMs sent guidance to impacted customers to disable auto-retries.

Next steps (owners):
- Jonas: reproduce regression locally and add CI coverage for kernel+quant combos (ETA: 1 week).
- Aditya: write runbook for emergency rollback and update oncall playbook (ETA: 3 days).
- Stephanie/Marissa: customer follow-ups + crediting & formal postmortem (ETA: draft in 24 hours).

We will schedule an executive readout tomorrow morning to review root cause, customer impact, and long-term controls (model validation, rollout gating by perf tests). Thank you to everyone who jumped in.

-Rishi
VP, Product Operations
[Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx]
